outputs.L1: A system for picking articles from storage containers into order containers uses a computer to manage and process picking orders and includes a picking station operating according to the goods-to-person principle. Articles selected by the computer are picked from the storage containers into conveyor bags. A suspension conveyor transports the conveyor bags to a packing location, where the articles assigned to a picking order are packed, and retrieves the conveyor bags into the order container assigned to that picking order. An order-container conveyor transports the order containers (boxes). The computer processes a first picking order to determine the number of articles to be picked at the picking station, such that the articles required to fulfill the first picking order are picked into the order container assigned to that order, while later articles are matched with and picked into a conveyor bag for the subsequent picking of further orders at the packing location.
outputs.L2: A computerized system manages and processes orders for transferring articles from storage bins into order containers at a picking station operating under the goods-to-person principle. Articles selected by the computer are removed from the storage bins and placed in conveyor bags. A suspension conveyor carries these bags to a packing area, where the articles associated with a particular picking order are packed, and the bags are emptied into the order container allocated to that order. An order-container conveyor moves the order containers, which may be boxes. For a first picking order, the computer calculates how many articles must be collected at the picking station. The required quantity for that first order is placed in its designated order container, while articles intended for subsequent orders are assigned to and picked into conveyor bags for later processing at the packing area.
outputs.L3:
The system processes article-picking orders using a computer-controlled goods-to-person picking station. At the station, selected articles are retrieved from storage containers and placed either into conveyor bags or directly into an order container.

A suspension conveyor transports the conveyor bags to a designated packing location, where the articles are used to complete the corresponding orders. At the same time, an order-container conveyor carries boxes assigned to the individual picking orders.

The computer coordinates both material flows. Articles associated with the first order are picked directly into the corresponding order container, while articles intended for subsequent orders are assigned to conveyor bags. These bags are then transported to the packing location, where their contents are packed into the appropriate order containers for final order fulfillment.
outputs.L4:
The system employs a computer-controlled good-to-person picking process in which storage containers holding inventory articles are automatically retrieved and delivered to a picking station. At the picking station, an operator or automated handling device removes the articles specified by the warehouse control system. Depending on the order to which each article belongs, the article is transferred either directly into an assigned order container or into a conveyor bag associated with a subsequent order.

Articles required for a first order are placed directly into the order container assigned to that order. Once all required articles have been collected, the completed container can be forwarded to packing, shipping, or another downstream processing area. At the same time, articles retrieved during the same picking sequence that are needed for later orders are placed into individually identifiable conveyor bags. These bags are carried by a suspension conveyor and temporarily buffered, sequenced, or routed to the appropriate packing location.

The control system coordinates the retrieval of storage containers, identifies the articles to be picked, and determines whether each article should be deposited into the current order container or into a conveyor bag. It also tracks the association between each bag and its corresponding order so that the articles can be delivered to the correct destination at the proper time. When the later order is ready for completion, the relevant bags are transported to the designated packing location, where their contents can be consolidated and packed.

By combining direct order picking with simultaneous sorting for future orders, the system makes more effective use of each presentation of a storage container. Articles for multiple orders can be handled during a single picking operation, reducing repeated storage-container retrievals, operator travel, and idle time. This coordinated process increases throughput, improves picking efficiency, and supports a more continuous flow of completed orders through the fulfillment facility.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a patent-style abstract describing a goods-to-person order-picking system that uses storage containers, conveyor bags, a suspension conveyor, order boxes, and computer-controlled batching of articles for multiple picking orders.
counterfactuals.output: A goods-to-person order-picking system includes a storage area containing articles in storage containers, a picking station, a suspension conveyor having individually controllable conveyor bags, and a packing area for order boxes. A computer-controlled warehouse management system groups article requirements from multiple picking orders into batches and causes selected storage containers to be transported to the picking station. At the picking station, articles are removed from the presented storage containers and loaded into assigned conveyor bags, each conveyor bag being associated with an article, a batch, or one or more picking orders. The suspension conveyor buffers, sorts, and selectively routes the conveyor bags to discharge stations in accordance with control instructions generated from the picking orders. At each discharge station, the articles are released from the conveyor bags into corresponding order boxes, with the computer system coordinating container presentation, bag assignment, conveyor routing, and box allocation to consolidate articles belonging to each picking order. Batching article retrieval across multiple orders reduces storage-container movements while automated bag sorting enables order-specific consolidation and increased picking throughput.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize an automated warehouse method in which items are picked at a goods-to-person station, temporarily placed in hanging conveyor bags, transported to packing, and consolidated into order containers.
counterfactuals.output:
An automated warehouse fulfills orders by:

1. Delivering storage containers to a goods-to-person picking station.
2. Picking required items and placing each item, or item group, into an identified hanging conveyor bag associated with an order.
3. Transporting the bags via an overhead conveyor to a packing area, with optional buffering and sorting.
4. Identifying and opening the bags at packing, then transferring their contents into the corresponding order container.
5. Consolidating all items for the same order in that container and releasing it for packing and shipment.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe a computer-controlled article-picking system that fulfills a first order directly in its assigned box while routing excess or later-picked items through conveyor bags for subsequent orders.
counterfactuals.output:
A computer-controlled article-picking system may include:

- **A central controller** that receives multiple customer orders, tracks inventory, schedules picking, and assigns each order a destination box.
- **Picking stations or automated pickers** that retrieve articles from storage.
- **A box conveyor** that presents the assigned box for the currently fulfilled, or first, order.
- **A bag conveyor** carrying individually identifiable bags, each associated by barcode or RFID with a later order or an intermediate buffer location.
- **A routing mechanism**—such as gates, chutes, or robotic diverters—controlled according to each article’s identity and order assignment.

During operation, articles needed for the first order are discharged directly into that order’s assigned box. If a picking operation produces additional articles, or if articles for later orders are picked at the same time, the controller diverts those articles into designated conveyor bags rather than the current box. The bags transport and temporarily segregate the articles until the corresponding later-order box reaches an unloading or consolidation station. The controller then identifies the bag, verifies its contents, and releases the articles into the proper box.

Thus, the first order is completed directly in its shipping box, while excess and advance-picked articles are buffered and routed in tracked conveyor bags for efficient fulfillment of subsequent orders.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a concise technical explanation of an order fulfillment system combining storage-bin retrieval, a picking station, an order-container conveyor, and an overhead pouch conveyor.
counterfactuals.output:
The order fulfillment system integrates four coordinated subsystems:

- **Storage-bin retrieval:** An automated storage and retrieval system delivers source bins containing inventory to a goods-to-person picking station.
- **Picking station:** Operators or robots remove the required quantities from each source bin. A control system identifies the target destination for every picked item.
- **Order-container conveyor:** Totes or cartons assigned to orders pass through the station on a conveyor. Items are placed directly into the appropriate container when it is available.
- **Overhead pouch conveyor:** Items whose order containers are not yet present, or items requiring temporary buffering, are placed into individually tracked pouches. The overhead system stores, sequences, and returns these items to a downstream consolidation point.

A warehouse control system synchronizes bin arrivals, container routing, pouch assignment, and order status. Direct picks minimize handling, while the pouch conveyor decouples picking from container availability and enables item sequencing. At consolidation, buffered items are released into their assigned order containers, which then proceed to verification, packing, and shipping.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a patent claim-style paragraph for a warehouse picking process where software determines item quantities, operators pick from presented storage containers, and articles for later orders are matched to suspended bags and consolidated at a packing location.
counterfactuals.output: 1. A computer-implemented method for fulfilling orders in a warehouse, the method comprising: determining, by a warehouse management system, respective quantities of articles required for a plurality of orders; causing storage containers holding the articles to be presented at a picking station; directing an operator to remove the determined quantities of the articles from the presented storage containers; associating articles designated for subsequently processed orders with respective suspended bags identified by the warehouse management system; placing the associated articles into the respective suspended bags; transporting the suspended bags to a packing location; and, at the packing location, consolidating the articles from each suspended bag with one or more additional articles associated with the corresponding order for packing and shipment.
counterfactuals.label: cf_5
